records.title: Thacker Pass and Rhyolite Ridge: two different paths to qualified material
records.answer: The two Nevada projects no longer fit a single undifferentiated development account. Thacker Pass reports major construction with a revised cost estimate; Rhyolite Ridge's inspected filing leaves its final investment decision undated. Their permits, environmental duties and future product acceptance must be followed separately.
records.scope: A comparison of two distinct Nevada projects, not a third project or one continuous mine. Thacker Pass is in Humboldt County and Rhyolite Ridge is in Esmeralda County. This parent contributes zero eligible projects; the two existing named dossiers retain their separate identity decisions.

sections.heading: Compare the projects without creating a third one
sections.text: The comparison connects two named developments that face a common question: how does an authorized resource become material a customer can repeatedly accept? It does not give them one location, one schedule or one operating status. NDEP describes Thacker Pass in Humboldt County; BLM's decision announcement identifies Rhyolite Ridge in Esmeralda County. The two project dossiers carry their own construction and environmental accounts. This parent is retained as Context with zero eligible-project contribution, while the regional Nevada reading addresses the wider receiving systems.

sections.heading: Thacker Pass has construction progress and a revised baseline
sections.text: Lithium Americas' November 12, 2026 update reports major construction continuing at Thacker Pass. Its Phase 1 capital estimate rose from US$2.93 billion to US$3.83 billion including contingency. Mechanical completion remained a late-2027 target, followed by ramp-up through 2028; craft-labor availability and installation productivity were among the identified risks. Those are the issuer's cost and schedule estimates, not completion certificates. Its transload terminal west of Winnemucca is another part of the reported delivery chain, rather than evidence that qualified lithium is already moving to customers.

sections.heading: Rhyolite Ridge still needs an investment decision in the inspected filing
sections.text: Ioneer's October 27, 2026 filing, for the quarter ended September 30, lists the final investment decision as TBA. Strategic partnering and refreshed economics remain conditions. The July agreements with KIND and Hyundai Engineering are non-binding, and reported road engineering and exploration-pad work are not a completed production plant. The roughly 36-month construction estimate depends on lead times and ordering; it is not a fixed production-start date. Ioneer's account of a district-court decision and subsequent appeal also remains attributed to the issuer, not an independently retrieved later judicial disposition.

sections.heading: Keep permit, processing and financing scopes distinct
sections.text: NDEP's Thacker Pass page records the February 25, 2022 air, water and mining permits, including the prohibition on mining below the water table. BLM's Rhyolite Ridge announcement concerns the plan of operations signed October 24, 2024 and announced October 29. DOE's respective environmental summaries describe processing facilities and associated infrastructure, excluding development and operation of the open pits. Those instruments cover different objects. The retained proposed-loan wording on the Thacker Pass DOE page does not update financing status, and neither a financing review nor a historical permit establishes later construction acceptance or compliance.

sections.heading: Environmental obligations and rights have separate evidence
sections.text: Rhyolite Ridge's habitat account includes the December 2022 rule listing Tiehm's buckwheat and designating critical habitat, effective January 17, 2023. A designation is not a later finding that mitigation succeeded. For Thacker Pass, Human Rights Watch and the ACLU's February 2025 research records objections concerning consultation, ancestral land and access to Peehee Mu'huh, alongside the company's response and its community-benefits agreement with the Fort McDermitt Paiute and Shoshone Tribe. These are attributed research findings and positions, not a new court judgment or evidence of universal consent. Commercial progress cannot settle either project's distinct environmental and rights questions.

sections.heading: Qualified supply needs evidence after construction
sections.text: Completion of named equipment, commissioning, compliant operation, material specification and customer acceptance are different transitions. A useful output account would identify the plant, product, quantity, quality criteria and reporting interval, then distinguish a first accepted lot from repeated delivery. Evidence from one project cannot qualify the other. The historical combined Phase 61 file and source-triggered Phase 63 gate remain unchanged; this comparison neither promotes their stage nor creates new governed files for the child dossiers. It also creates no Phase 60 identity or dated appointment.

next_artifacts: For Thacker Pass: dated completion and commissioning instruments for the named systems, with compliance and product qualification assessed separately.
For Rhyolite Ridge: a dated final investment decision and binding commitments, followed by project-specific construction and commissioning records.
For each project independently: compatible output and customer-acceptance evidence, alongside environmental monitoring and affected-community accounts.
